title: USB protocol (enumeration and transfers)
summary: USB (Universal Serial Bus) is a host-controlled serial bus. Enumeration: device connects → host detects (via pull-up on D+/D-) → host sends reset → host reads device descriptor → host assigns address → host reads configuration descriptor → host loads driver → device ready. Transfer types: Control (setup + data + status, for enumeration/config), Bulk (large data, error-checked, no timing guarantee), Interrupt (small data, periodic, guaranteed latency), Isochronous (streaming, guaranteed bandwidth, no retry).

structure.meaning: 1. Device connects (pull-up on D+/D-). 2. Host detects, sends reset. 3. Host reads device descriptor (address 0). 4. Host assigns address (SET_ADDRESS). 5. Host reads config descriptor. 6. Host sets configuration (SET_CONFIGURATION). 7. Device ready.
Setup (8 bytes: bmRequestType, bRequest, wValue, wIndex, wLength) + Data (optional, wLength bytes) + Status (zero-length packet, opposite direction).
Large data, error-checked (CRC16), retried on error. No timing guarantee. Used for storage, printers.
Small data, periodic (polling interval), guaranteed latency. Used for keyboards, mice.
Guaranteed bandwidth, no retry (errors not corrected). Used for audio, video.
Endpoint 0 = control. Endpoints 1-15 = data (IN/OUT). Each endpoint has a type and max packet size.
Low (1.5 Mbps), Full (12 Mbps), High (480 Mbps), Super (5 Gbps), Super+ (10 Gbps), Super++ (20 Gbps).

notes: USB is host-controlled: the host initiates all transfers.
USB devices are identified by vendor ID (VID) and product ID (PID) (assigned by USB-IF).
USB hubs enable tree topology (up to 127 devices per host controller).
USB-C is the latest connector (reversible, up to 40 Gbps with Thunderbolt 4).
USB is the universal peripheral interface (keyboards, mice, storage, cameras, etc.).
